correctness.rationale: The complete 102-tetrahedron complex reconstructs f=(17,119,204,102). The embedded certificate proves an integral basis of ker d2 and a left inverse. In that basis the tetrahedral boundary matrix has determinant of absolute value 2, so H2 is Z/2. A quotient detector gives an exhaustive lower-bound test on every support of size at most seven: no support through six works and exactly five seven-subsets survive. Each of those five is then verified as an induced connected orientable closed seven-vertex surface with Euler characteristic zero, and its explicit integral fundamental cycle has nonzero quotient detector.

value.rationale: B3 has pure torsion in degree two, so an exact embedded representative problem is more informative than a Betti-number calculation. The nonzero order-two class first appears at seven vertices, exactly the absolute minimum possible for a triangulated torus, and the complete minimum layer consists of exactly five induced vertex-minimal tori. This is a natural finite systolic classification tied to the topology and incidence structure of the small triangulation.
